moments.title: Luther's New Testament
moments.body:
Luther translates the New Testament into German in 11 weeks while in hiding at the Wartburg.

He draws on East Central German chancellery usage.
moments.takeaway: A theological translation became a literary instrument for shaping a vernacular.

moments.title: Complete Luther Bible
moments.body: The complete German Bible is published, helped by movable-type printing. Its language spreads rapidly across the Protestant lands.
moments.takeaway: Religious upheaval and print technology produced lasting linguistic standardisation.

moments.title: Brothers Grimm's Marchen
moments.body:
The Grimms publish their tale collection.

Their later Deutsches Worterbuch project is begun in 1838 and only completed in 1961.
moments.takeaway: Romantic-era philology gave the German language new tools for its own study.

now.title: German today
now.body: German is the most widely spoken native language in the EU (about 95 million speakers). Spelling reform (1996, revised 2006) and gender-inclusive writing debates continue.
now.open_questions: How will written German respond to inclusive writing debates? How does Swiss German diglossia evolve in digital contexts?

items.reflection: Even after centuries of standardisation, German continues to be the focus of language reform debates.

moments.title: Critique of Pure Reason
moments.body: Kant's first critique restructures epistemology by distinguishing what can be known from how the mind structures experience.
moments.takeaway: A single book set the agenda of European philosophy for two centuries.

moments.title: What is Enlightenment?
moments.body: Kant's essay defines enlightenment as 'man's emergence from his self-imposed nonage'.
moments.takeaway: Short essays can serve as the public face of long philosophical projects.

moments.title: Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit
moments.body:
Hegel completes the Phenomenology as Napoleon's army approaches.

His dialectical method will shape Marx, theology and 20th-century philosophy.
moments.takeaway: German Idealism developed in close proximity to political upheaval.

now.title: Philosophy in German today
now.body: Frankfurt School traditions, analytic philosophy in German universities and ongoing translation projects keep German philosophy active in current debates.
now.open_questions: How are 19th-century concepts being reread for contemporary problems in technology and ethics?

items.reflection: A small Prussian university town produced philosophy that reshaped a continent's thinking.

moments.title: Klemperer's LTI
moments.body: Klemperer publishes a philological study of the language of the Third Reich, drawing on diaries kept through the war.
moments.takeaway: Linguistic documentation under dictatorship produced a study read for generations.

moments.title: Gunter Grass's Die Blechtrommel
moments.body:
The novel addresses Nazism, war and post-war silence from inside the Polish-German borderlands.

Grass's later Nobel Prize comes in 1999.
moments.takeaway: Post-war German writing wrestled with questions earlier institutions had avoided.

moments.title: Reunification
moments.body:
The Berlin Wall fell in November 1989; full political unification followed on 3 October 1990.

German literature and language absorb the East-West encounter.
moments.takeaway: A political event reshaped what 'German' meant institutionally and culturally.

now.title: German letters today
now.body: Contemporary writers (Daniel Kehlmann, Jenny Erpenbeck, Sasa Stanisic) address migration, memory and Europe's recent past. Translation flows are robust.
now.open_questions: How will writing in German evolve as the country's demographics diversify?

items.reflection: Some of Germany's most influential 20th-century literature came from writers who had to leave or who returned from exile.

moments.title: First Duden dictionary
moments.body: Duden's orthographic dictionary becomes the de facto standard reference, reinforced by the Orthographic Conference of 1901.
moments.takeaway: Standardisation of writing required private and state cooperation.

moments.title: Spelling reform agreed
moments.body:
Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Liechtenstein and Luxembourg agree a spelling reform implemented in stages.

Major newspapers reverse and re-adopt aspects through the 2000s; the revised version is settled in 2006.
moments.takeaway: Coordinated language reform across multiple states is politically difficult.

moments.title: Capital eszett accepted
moments.body:
The capital ss (uppercase eszett) is officially accepted.

Gender-neutral writing remains contested.
moments.takeaway: Orthographic change continues into the 21st century.

now.title: German varieties today
now.body: Swiss German diglossia persists; Austrian German has its own standard variety. Dialect maintenance varies sharply by region.
now.open_questions: Will digital communication accelerate convergence or maintain dialect distinctness?

items.reflection: What we call 'German' is a family of related standards and dialects, not a single uniform language.

moments.title: Luther posts 95 Theses
moments.body: Luther's challenge to the sale of indulgences is traditionally said to have been posted on the Schlosskirche door on 31 October 1517.
moments.takeaway: Single documents can rewire centuries.

moments.title: Diet of Worms
moments.body: Luther refuses to recant: 'Here I stand. I can do no other.' He is declared an outlaw.

quote.text: Hier stehe ich. Ich kann nicht anders.

moments.takeaway: Public confrontation with empire became a defining German Protestant moment.

moments.title: Peace of Augsburg
moments.body: The principle of 'cuius regio, eius religio' allows rulers to choose Lutheranism or Catholicism for their realms.
moments.takeaway: Religious choice became a state-level decision.

now.title: Reformation today
now.body: 2017 marked the 500th anniversary of the Reformation across German states. Ecumenical relations have transformed since.
now.open_questions: How are Reformation legacies being reread in Catholic-Protestant marriages and parishes?

items.reflection: Modern German identity is impossible to understand without the Reformation.

moments.title: Defenestration of Prague
moments.body: Catholic regents are thrown from a Prague Castle window. The act ignites a 30-year European war.
moments.takeaway: Wars can begin with a window.

moments.title: Peace of Westphalia
moments.body: The peace treaties end the Thirty Years' War, killing perhaps a third of central Europe's population.
moments.takeaway: Westphalia is often cited as the birthplace of modern state sovereignty.

moments.title: Holy Roman Empire dissolved
moments.body: Under Napoleonic pressure, the millennium-old Empire is abolished.
moments.takeaway: Symbolic political entities can persist long after losing power.

now.title: Westphalia today
now.body: International relations theory still cites Westphalian sovereignty. Climate and migration policy challenge the model.
now.open_questions: Has the Westphalian state system reached its limits?

items.reflection: Modern Europe's map and political vocabulary date partly from this war's ending.

moments.title: Die Leiden des jungen Werthers
moments.body: Goethe's epistolary novel becomes a European sensation; readers reportedly dress like Werther and (perhaps) imitate his suicide.
moments.takeaway: Romantic literature could shape behaviour.

moments.title: Faust I
moments.body: Goethe's verse drama on knowledge, desire and damnation defines the German literary canon.
moments.takeaway: A nation's defining work can take its author 60 years.

moments.title: Goethe dies
moments.body: Goethe finishes Faust II shortly before his death.
moments.takeaway: Long careers can converge on single works.

now.title: Goethe today
now.body: Goethe-Institut runs cultural diplomacy worldwide. Faust remains a Theater repertoire mainstay.
now.open_questions: What is Goethe to readers outside Germany now?

items.reflection: Goethe became Germany's Shakespeare in his own lifetime.

moments.title: Bismarck becomes minister-president
moments.body: Bismarck promises 'blood and iron' rather than speeches as the means of German unification.
moments.takeaway: Realpolitik became a German export.

moments.title: German Empire proclaimed
moments.who: Wilhelm I, Hall of Mirrors at Versailles
moments.body: The German Empire is declared in defeated France's palace.
moments.takeaway: Unification was achieved through war, not federation.

moments.title: Year of three emperors
moments.who: Wilhelm I, Friedrich III, Wilhelm II
moments.body: Three emperors reign in a single year; Wilhelm II's accession changes Germany's trajectory.
moments.takeaway: Imperial succession could be unstable.

now.title: Unification's memory
now.body: Bismarck remains a controversial figure. The Kulturkampf against Catholicism is studied as a precedent for later policy.
now.open_questions: How do we narrate national unification ethically?

items.reflection: Modern Germany was born by force in someone else's palace.

moments.title: Weimar constitution
moments.body: Post-war Germany adopts a parliamentary constitution including women's suffrage.
moments.takeaway: Defeat produced democratic experiment.

moments.title: Hyperinflation peaks
moments.body: By November 1923, a loaf of bread costs 200 billion marks. The Rentenmark stabilises prices.
moments.takeaway: Money lost meaning in months.

moments.title: Weimar ends
moments.body: After the 1929 crash, Weimar coalitions collapse. Hitler is appointed chancellor in January 1933.
moments.takeaway: Economic crisis enabled fascism's rise.

now.title: Weimar's lessons
now.body: Weimar's collapse is repeatedly cited in democratic theory. Cabaret culture, Bauhaus and German cinema (Murnau, Lang) shaped global modernism.
now.open_questions: Are present democracies repeating Weimar's mistakes?

items.reflection: Weimar was modernism and crisis at once.

moments.title: Bauhaus founded
moments.body: Gropius merges Weimar's arts and crafts schools into the Bauhaus.
moments.takeaway: Design education was a deliberate political project.

moments.title: Move to Dessau
moments.body: Political pressure forces the school to relocate; Gropius designs a new campus.
moments.takeaway: Modernist institutions were politically targeted.

moments.title: Bauhaus closed
moments.body: The school is dissolved. Many faculty leave for the United States.
moments.takeaway: Forced migration spread German modernism worldwide.

now.title: Bauhaus globalisation
now.body: Tel Aviv's White City is a UNESCO heritage Bauhaus quarter. Bauhaus design principles continue in product design and architecture.
now.open_questions: How do we hold Bauhaus's modernist promise alongside its political fragility?

items.reflection: A 14-year-old school reshaped 20th-century built environments.

moments.title: Hitler becomes chancellor
moments.body: Hitler is appointed chancellor on 30 January 1933. The Reichstag fire (February) and Enabling Act (March) consolidate dictatorship.
moments.takeaway: Democracy can be dismantled within weeks.

moments.title: Nuremberg Laws
moments.body: Antisemitic laws strip German Jews of citizenship and rights.
moments.takeaway: Legal frameworks enabled state racism.

moments.title: Kristallnacht
moments.body: Coordinated attacks on Jewish synagogues, businesses and homes on 9-10 November.
moments.takeaway: Violence against German Jews escalated visibly years before mass deportation.

now.title: Memory today
now.body: Vergangenheitsbewaltigung ('coming to terms with the past') is a foundational German political concept. Holocaust education is compulsory in German schools.
now.open_questions: How does memory work pass to generations with no living witnesses?

items.reflection: Germany's national identity has been rebuilt around honest reckoning with the worst of its history.

moments.title: Wannsee Conference
moments.body: Senior officials coordinate the 'Final Solution' to the Jewish question.
moments.takeaway: The Holocaust was bureaucratically planned.

moments.title: Auschwitz liberated
moments.body: Auschwitz-Birkenau is liberated on 27 January 1945, now International Holocaust Remembrance Day.
moments.takeaway: The scale of the camps became known to the world in 1945.

moments.title: First Stolpersteine laid
moments.body: Demnig begins laying brass cobblestones commemorating Holocaust victims at their last freely chosen residences. Over 100,000 are now installed across Europe.
moments.takeaway: Public memory can be quietly distributed across streets.

now.title: Holocaust memory today
now.body: Yad Vashem, Berlin's Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe (2005) and major museums anchor remembrance. Antisemitism in Germany is rising again.
now.open_questions: How does memory work continue without survivors?

items.reflection: Stolpersteine put history under your feet on the way to the shops.

moments.title: Germany divided
moments.body: The Federal Republic (BRD) and German Democratic Republic (DDR) are founded in 1949.
moments.takeaway: Cold War geography ran through German towns.

moments.title: Berlin Wall built
moments.body: Beginning 13 August 1961, East Germany erects a wall through Berlin to stop emigration.
moments.takeaway: The wall divided neighbourhoods overnight.

moments.title: Wall falls
moments.body: On 9 November 1989, East Germany's border guards open the wall after a confused press conference announcement.
moments.takeaway: Empires can end in confused press briefings.

now.title: Reunification's legacy
now.body: East-West inequalities persist. AfD vote shares are higher in former East. Ostalgie persists as cultural memory.
now.open_questions: When does the East-West distinction stop being meaningful?

items.reflection: Reunification was political; cultural integration took longer.

moments.title: Merkel becomes chancellor
moments.body: Merkel becomes Germany's first female chancellor; she will serve 16 years.
moments.takeaway: Political stability shaped Europe.

moments.title: Refugee policy
moments.body: Merkel keeps the German border open to Syrian refugees; 'Wir schaffen das' ('we can do this').
moments.takeaway: Single political moments reshape decades of demography.

moments.title: Zeitenwende
moments.body: Following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Scholz announces a turning point in German foreign and defence policy.
moments.takeaway: Wars force national reorientation.

now.title: Germany today
now.body: Energy transition, AfD rise and Ukraine support shape current politics. Germany is the EU's largest economy.
now.open_questions: What does German leadership of Europe look like next?

items.reflection: Germany's post-war stability has been continuously remade.

moments.title: Die Verwandlung
moments.body: Gregor Samsa wakes up as a giant insect. The German-language novella is one of the 20th century's most-read fictions.
moments.takeaway: A single sentence can open a literary world.

moments.title: Kafka dies
moments.body: Kafka dies of tuberculosis at 40, leaving most novels unpublished.
moments.takeaway: Many definitive works were never authorised by their author.

moments.title: Posthumous novels
moments.body: Brod ignores Kafka's instruction to burn his manuscripts and publishes Der Prozess (1925), Das Schloss (1926) and Amerika (1927).
moments.takeaway: Some literary careers are made by editors.

now.title: Kafka now
now.body: Kafka's archive ownership has been disputed (Israel vs Germany). Centenary year (2024) renewed interest.
now.open_questions: Where does the German-Jewish literary heritage belong?

items.reflection: Kafka wrote in German from Prague, a city now in a country that does not have German as official language.

moments.title: Der Zauberberg
moments.body: Mann's novel set in a Swiss sanatorium is a portrait of pre-WWI Europe.
moments.takeaway: The novel could diagnose a continent.

moments.title: Mann wins Nobel
moments.body: Mann wins the Nobel Prize for Literature.
moments.takeaway: German letters held Nobel prestige before Hitler.

moments.title: Mann exiled
moments.body: Mann emigrates after Nazi takeover, settling later in California.
moments.takeaway: Literary culture was scattered by exile.

now.title: German literature today
now.body: Jenny Erpenbeck won the 2024 International Booker. Contemporary German fiction wrestles with migration, memory and Europe.
now.open_questions: Who counts as a 'German' writer in 21st-century Europe?

items.reflection: Some of 20th-century German literature's greatest writers wrote in exile.

moments.title: Communist Manifesto
moments.body: Marx and Engels publish 'Das Kommunistische Manifest' weeks before the Year of Revolutions.
moments.takeaway: Political philosophy travelled through pamphlets.

moments.title: Das Kapital volume 1
moments.body: Marx publishes the first volume of his critique of political economy; further volumes are completed posthumously by Engels.
moments.takeaway: Single books have launched political movements.

moments.title: Marx dies
moments.body: Marx dies in Highgate Cemetery. His writings influence parties, regimes and academia worldwide.
moments.takeaway: Few thinkers have had such durable political consequences.

now.title: Marx today
now.body: Marxist analysis returned to mainstream economics after 2008. His writings remain widely taught.
now.open_questions: How is 19th-century class analysis renewed for the 21st century?

items.reflection: A German philosopher living in London shaped a 20th century he never saw.

moments.title: Thus Spoke Zarathustra
moments.body: Nietzsche writes his philosophical novel in bursts of intense work.
moments.takeaway: German philosophy could read like literature.

moments.title: Nietzsche collapses
moments.body: Nietzsche collapses on a Turin street, apparently embracing a flogged horse. He never recovers.
moments.takeaway: Some thinkers leave their work mid-sentence.

moments.title: Nietzsche dies
moments.body: Nietzsche dies in his sister Elisabeth's care. She edits his unfinished work and aligns it with antisemitic politics.
moments.takeaway: Posthumous reputations can be manipulated by family.

now.title: Nietzsche now
now.body: Contemporary reception separates Nietzsche's writings from Elisabeth's redaction. His prose continues to influence philosophy, theology and literary criticism.
now.open_questions: How do we read a philosopher whose name was weaponised?

items.reflection: Nietzsche's afterlife shows how thinkers can be reshaped after death.

moments.title: Einstein's annus mirabilis
moments.body: Einstein publishes four papers, including special relativity and E=mc².
moments.takeaway: Single years can reshape physics.

moments.title: Planck wins Nobel
moments.body: Planck wins the Nobel for quantum theory work begun in 1900.
moments.takeaway: Major prizes follow decades behind discovery.

moments.title: Einstein leaves Germany
moments.body: Einstein settles at Princeton's Institute for Advanced Study. Many other Jewish German scientists also emigrate.
moments.takeaway: Nazi Germany lost scientific leadership through emigration.

now.title: German science today
now.body: Max Planck Institutes continue research. Germany leads European industrial science but post-Nazi exile costs remain.
now.open_questions: Could Germany regain its early 20th-century scientific dominance?

items.reflection: Antisemitism cost Germany the science that built the atomic age.

moments.title: Institute for Social Research
moments.body: The institute that becomes the Frankfurt School is founded.
moments.takeaway: Critical theory had an institutional base.

moments.title: Dialectic of Enlightenment
moments.body: Written in California exile, the book argues that Enlightenment reason has produced its opposite.
moments.takeaway: Exiled philosophers wrote about modernity's failures.

moments.title: Theory of Communicative Action
moments.body: Habermas's late work elaborates a theory of public reason for post-war democracies.
moments.takeaway: Frankfurt School thought continued through generations.

now.title: Critical theory today
now.body: Adorno's cultural criticism is reread for social media analysis. Habermas continues to publish in his 90s.
now.open_questions: How do we adapt Frankfurt School thought to platform capitalism?

items.reflection: A school formed in Weimar Germany shaped American academia for half a century.

moments.title: Die Dreigroschenoper
moments.body: The Threepenny Opera premieres in Berlin; 'Mack the Knife' becomes a standard.
moments.takeaway: Popular theatre could be theoretically ambitious.

moments.title: Brecht exiled
moments.body: Brecht flees Germany, eventually reaching the US. He is later called before the House Un-American Activities Committee.
moments.takeaway: Theatrical innovation was politically vulnerable.

moments.title: Berliner Ensemble founded
moments.who: Brecht and Helene Weigel, East Berlin
moments.body: Brecht returns to East Germany to direct the Berliner Ensemble.
moments.takeaway: Exiled artists made hard choices about return.

now.title: Brecht's theatre today
now.body: Verfremdung techniques shape contemporary political theatre, from Hamilton to TikTok performance.
now.open_questions: What is the digital equivalent of Brecht's alienation effect?

items.reflection: Brecht wanted theatre that didn't let you forget you were watching it.

moments.title: Die Ausgewanderten
moments.body: Sebald's hybrid essay-fiction examines Jewish exile from a German perspective.
moments.takeaway: German post-war writing reckons with absence.

moments.title: Austerlitz
moments.body: Sebald's novel of a Kindertransport survivor's late discovery of his past is published months before his death.
moments.takeaway: Some careers culminate just before their end.

moments.title: Sebald dies
moments.body: Sebald, a long-term professor in England, dies in a car crash at 57.
moments.takeaway: Some of the most important post-war German writing was done abroad.

now.title: Sebald now
now.body: Sebald's photographs-in-text technique influences contemporary writers (Olga Tokarczuk, Maggie Nelson).
now.open_questions: How does writing about the Holocaust evolve as witnesses die?

items.reflection: Memory can be written in pictures as much as words.

moments.title: Sein und Zeit
moments.body: Heidegger publishes 'Being and Time', a foundational work of 20th-century continental philosophy.
moments.takeaway: Difficult philosophy still finds enormous influence.

moments.title: Heidegger joins NSDAP
moments.body: Heidegger becomes rector of Freiburg and joins the Nazi party, in a step he never adequately repudiates.
moments.takeaway: Major thinkers are not immune to fascism.

moments.title: Black Notebooks published
moments.body: Heidegger's private notebooks reveal antisemitism embedded in his philosophy.
moments.takeaway: Posthumous publication can reshape reputations.

now.title: Heidegger today
now.body: Debates continue over how to teach Heidegger given his politics.
now.open_questions: Can philosophy be separated from its philosopher?

items.reflection: Heidegger's case is the central test of separating work from worker.

moments.title: Austria-Hungary
moments.body: The Ausgleich creates the dual monarchy. Vienna becomes a multilingual cultural capital.
moments.takeaway: German is one of many languages of central European empire.

moments.title: Anschluss
moments.body: Germany annexes Austria. Most Austrians initially welcome the move.
moments.takeaway: Linguistic kinship eased political annexation.

moments.title: Austrian neutrality
moments.body: The State Treaty restores Austrian sovereignty with permanent neutrality.
moments.takeaway: Cold War settlements created new national identities.

now.title: German-speaking world today
now.body: Austria, Switzerland, Liechtenstein and parts of Belgium and Italy keep German official. Common spelling reform coordinates orthography.
now.open_questions: How does German evolve across so many states?

items.reflection: There is no single German country.

moments.title: Bach's musical offering
moments.body: Bach improvises on a theme set by Frederick the Great, later expanding it into Das Musikalische Opfer.
moments.takeaway: German musical tradition included royal-court improvisation.

moments.title: Parsifal premiered
moments.body: Wagner's last opera consecrates the Bayreuth Festspielhaus's purpose-built role.
moments.takeaway: Wagner shaped both German music and German nationalism.

moments.title: Schoenberg's twelve-tone method
moments.body: Schoenberg breaks with tonality, founding serialism. He emigrates in 1933.
moments.takeaway: German-language music shaped modernism and was scattered by exile.

now.title: Tradition today
now.body: Berlin Philharmonic, Vienna Philharmonic and Salzburg Festival anchor a global classical industry. Composer-historians question Wagner's politics.
now.open_questions: Can a national musical tradition reckon with its complicity?

items.reflection: Few cultures have produced as much music as the German-speaking world.
